reason: Underwater low-light environments suffer from illumination attenuation, color distortion, and detail degradation, which severely affect visual perception performance. This paper proposes an unsupervised integrated framework, termed EUMNet, for joint underwater image enhancement and object detection. An end-to-end collaborative architecture is designed to enable the enhancement process to be guided by semantic cues from the detection branch. A frequency decoupling strategy and a bidirectional cross-layer fusion mechanism are introduced to achieve global illumination correction and local detail restoration. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves both image quality and detection accuracy.
title: EUMNet: An End-to-End Framework for Underwater Low-Light Image Enhancement and Aquatic Object Detection
